articles.title: Week 4 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Ollie Gordon II, Braelon Allen, Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: Fantasy managers could probably use some good news after an injury-riddled start to Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Fantasy managers could probably use some good news after an injury-riddled start to Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.

Here's the best we can muster: Bye weeks don't start until Week 5.

So, hey, things could be ( and unfortunately will be ) even harder to manage if ( when ) navigating around both the injury-bug attacks and empty slots on the schedule. For now, let's find some plug-and-play replacements available in 50-plus percent of leagues (per FantasyPros) for some of these injured stars.

Ollie Gordon II, RB, Miami Dolphins (1% Rostered)

The Dolphins reportedly lost star running back De'Von Achane to a knee injury for the season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter . That's a crushing blow for a rebuilding roster that was already woefully short on playmakers.

In the fantasy world, though, it's also opportunity's knock for the proverbial next man up—in this case Gordon, who immediately handled 17 carries and three targets in Achane's absence.

That kind of volume is impossible to ignore. It's also maybe the only thing propping up Gordon, who is averaging fewer than three yards per carry for the second time in as many NFL seasons.

Still, volume can trump efficiency in fantasy, as Gordon himself just showed. Those 20 touches Sunday yielded 55 scrimmage yards and a score, making him a top-15 fantasy running back this week.

Braelon Allen, RB, New York Jets (17% Rostered)

Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury Sunday and never returned. The chance that Hall misses any time moving forward should make Allen a priority target this week.

Allen had already been involved even when Hall was healthy. Allen handled 10 carries in the season-opener (and turned them into 40 yards) and scored a touchdown in Week 2.

He has also impressed in spot duty before. As a rookie fourth-rounder in 2024, he delivered 334 rushing yards, 19 receptions for 148 yards and three touchdowns.

Now, Allen won't hold fantasy value beyond being a handcuff if Hall avoids any absences, so there is a bit of risk in adding him. That said, Allen might fill feature-back duties if Hall is shelved, so the reward outweighs that risk and then some.

Kirk Cousins, QB, Las Vegas Raiders (17% Rostered)

With injuries piling up at the quarterback position, there's a decent chance you could find yourself in the market for a stopgap signal-caller.

How good would it feel to fill that void with a quarterback who has thrown three touchdowns in every game he's played this season? Sounds too good to be true, doesn't it? Well, apparently not, as Cousins' first three contests with the Raiders have all featured three touchdown strikes.

Can he keep this up for an entire season? Certainly not. But could he stretch this hot streak out for another couple of weeks? Maybe. He has been this productive so far, so who's to say this streak is guaranteed to end in Week 4? No one you should take fantasy advice from, that's for sure.

Don't hold Cousins' struggles over the past two seasons in Atlanta against him. He has historically been a quality quarterback, and he is posting some of the best stats you'll find at the position. His nine touchdown passes are tied for the league lead, and his 67.4 completion percentage sits eight-highest among the 16 quarterbacks with 90-plus pass attempts.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Brock Bowers, Emeka Egbuka among top risers, fallers in Week 3
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through his top risers and fallers following Week 3 for fantasy football.
articles.body:
As I write this on Sunday night, 15 of 16 Week 3 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the season is sort of starting to round into shape. Sort of. There were promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that changed our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 4.

Across a number of platforms, I made a bold prediction before the season that Brock Bowers would break the single-season receptions record of 149, set by Michael Thomas in 2019. The Raiders tight end missed the first two games ... and now he's right on track to do exactly that. It was start-to-finish dominance from Bowers, who some feared would be hampered or limited in his Week 3 return. Instead, he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown. If anything, it looks better for Bowers than it did before the season, because of how well Kirk Cousins is playing. The veteran QB has thrown three touchdowns in each of the first three games, with Bowers snagging the third score on Sunday. Clearly 100% healthy, in a passing attack that's been shockingly productive, with a quarterback who's led last year's worst team to a 3-0 start ... Bowers has immediately assumed his place as fantasy's top tight end and arguably one of the best position-adjusted players in the game.

After two straight games of single-digit fantasy points, managers were starting to panic on Drake London ... but it seems Michael Penix Jr. has returned to save the day. In his first start of the year, Penix found London nine times on 10 targets for an absolutely absurd 194 receiving yards. It was a career high for the 25-year-old receiver and came on a day when Bijan Robinson also rushed for 194 yards. While this might have been more of an indictment of the Packers ' defense than anything, it's clear that Penix is better for London's value than Cooper Rush or Jake Strand. By an order of magnitude. We'll see how the Atlanta offense fares in New Orleans in Week 4, but London is back to fringe WR1 territory after his dominant TNF performance.

While Harold Fannin Jr.'s Week 2 fantasy output of 7.9 points was relatively disappointing, he did catch five balls on six targets for 54 yards in that game, which is plenty solid for a tight end. In Week 3, he took all those numbers up a notch, logging seven snags for 51 yards on nine targets ... but far more importantly, he scored a pair of touchdowns to finish with 20.6 fantasy points. This was what managers expected when they drafted him in the upper-half of TE1 territory in the summer. If we turn a half-blind eye to Week 1, Fannin's first game with Deshaun Watson , he's now totaled 12 catches for 105 yards and two scores on 15 targets the last two weeks. Given the nature of the offense and the quarterback room, Fannin might not be the most consistent TE1 in fantasy, but Week 3 solidified that he does belong in that TE1 conversation. You can start him with relative confidence again.

While Jaylen Warren still has not found the end zone this season, he has been one of the most consistently productive dual-threat running backs in the entire league, and broke out on the ground on Sunday. Warren galloped for 127 yards on 17 carries in Week 3, while adding three catches for 49 yards as well. It was his third straight game with 40+ rushing yards and 25+ receiving yards. There's one other player that can match that claim ... and his name is Jahmyr Gibbs . Obviously, Warren's ceiling is much lower than Gibbs', and the lack of touchdowns is concerning. But Warren has played three potentially tough matchups and established an impressive floor throughout. As far as reliable RB2s or high-end FLEX plays, Warren looks like one of the better options and will get even better for fantasy as the touchdowns come through.

It's clear that whatever Kellen Moore is doing for Tyler Shough, it's working. At least for fantasy. Forget "strong streamer" or "good superflex QB2" or even "spot-start QB1" ... Shough is making a strong case as a top-tier quarterback in fantasy. He's scored 22+ fantasy points in all three games this season, with 250+ passing yards in each and a total of eight touchdown passes and one score on the ground. In fact, Shough is the first QB since Josh Allen in 2022 to log 250+ passing yards, multiple total touchdowns and 22+ fantasy points in each of the first three weeks of a season. The year before, the only players to do it were Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady . Shough has also rushed for more yards in each successive game this year (with 36 on a single carry on Sunday), and leads the entire NFL in attempts (132) and completions (91), and is second to Bryce Young in passing yards (917). His current pace? That'd be 5,196 yards and 45 touchdowns passing. The Saints are playing fun and competitive football, and Shough is both a beneficiary and a big reason why. Until further notice, he should be considered not just a QB1, but squarely in the next tier of quarterback stars behind Josh Allen (a la Mahomes and Joe Burrow ).

Wow. Drake Maye was in this section of last week's column, where I said that he "could get into a barn-burner against the Jaguars ... so you're probably still starting him (and hoping) for at least another couple games." That hope came crashing to the ground in Week 3. Maye is lost. Unequivocally discombobulated and frankly incapable of NFL-level quarterback play right now. I watched the entire Pats-Jags game on Sunday and saw nothing redeeming from the third-year QB, who is now up to six giveaways and one touchdown through three games. In the absence of Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte — with whom Maye had uncanny downfield connections last season — as well as an injured A.J. Brown , it just seems like the Patriots quarterback has zero chemistry, zero confidence and zero comprehension of opposing defenses. Last season's QB2 overall is simply not present right now, so if you're making lineup decisions involving Maye, forget about last season entirely. Next week, he faces the Bills, which means he'll likely be throwing a lot ... but I'd be hesitant to trust him in any matchup right now. At best, he's a fringe QB1 in good matchups. More likely, he's a park-on-the-bench asset we can hope improves when Brown eventually returns.

Oddly, Emeka Egbuka has been one of fantasy's most consistent wide receivers. The problem is that he's scored 8.8, 8.8 and 8.7 fantasy points, which, while impressively consistent, is not useful in starting lineups. Moreover, he has yet to top five catches or 63 yards in a game and had just three catches for 16 yards two weeks ago. None of this is WR1 material, and it's not great WR2 material either. But to make matters worse, Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb on Sunday and is likely to miss some time. That leaves Egbuka and the rest of Tampa Bay with undrafted, six-year Kansas quarterback Jalon Daniels in the interim. And while Mayfield hasn't been great, it's pretty tough to imagine Egbuka suddenly breaking out with an unheralded backup quarterback. Candidly, nothing about the Buccaneers offense has been encouraging through three weeks, so no matter how much time Mayfield misses, the outlook is currently grim for Egbuka's fantasy managers. Given the talent we saw early last season, he's worth holding on your bench. But he should not see your starting lineup for the foreseeable future.

It's been quite the yo-yo start to the season for Jaylen Waddle. He was non-existent in Week 1. Then he was the entire offense in Week 2. And on Sunday night, he did see seven targets but caught just two of them for 10 yards. The Broncos offense was a disaster for most of the game, before finding a small resurgence in the second half, and confidence in Davis Webb 's play-calling is ... less than a mile high. When it comes to Waddle specifically, it's less than an inch high. So far, a career-low 38.2% of his routes are in-breaking and 17.1% of his routes are deep (second-highest mark of his career). It feels like he's getting the Marvin Harrison Jr. treatment, and in two of three weeks, it has not worked. Here's a quick hint, Davis: Waddle's averaging 2.9 yards per route run on in-breaking routes and 1.4 YPRR on every other route. And in his career in Miami , he averaged 2.7 yards per route run on in-breakers and 1.9 on all others. If the offensive minds in Denver don't start utilizing Waddle where he's best — tearing up the intermediate middle of the field — and continue to run him straight and deep, he's going to be extremely frustrating for fantasy.

I said leading into last week that it was essentially now-or-never for Quinshon Judkins, in an extremely juicy matchup with the Panthers. And while Judkins did end up rushing for 70 yards ... that's pretty much all he did. It took him 18 carries to get there (3.9 yards per carry) and his two receptions on the day went for just nine yards. As a result, he finished with single-digit fantasy points for the third straight week, in the second game the Browns managed to win. If Judkins can't hit double digits in (rare) Browns wins against beatable defenses, when or where can we ever expect him to do so? The answer, until further notice, is nowhere and never. At least not predictably. Judkins has been extremely inefficient and has yet to find the end zone through three weeks. He's still dominating carries in the offense, so we can't drop him, but that almost makes him more problematic for fantasy. For now, park him on your bench, find an option with higher upside if you can and hope that he finds a second gear (and a touchdown or two) in the coming weeks.

articles.title: New Jayden Daniels Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Commanders' Game vs. Colts in London
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has a chance to return to action from his elbow injury in Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts in London.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has a chance to return to action from his elbow injury in Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts in London.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer that Daniels will "more than likely" travel with the team to the United Kingdom when they leave on Tuesday night. Quinn said that he "doesn't know yet whether Daniels will play in six days," but Breer noted that this latest development indicates that the signal-caller "isn't far off."

The news comes after general manager Adam Peters said Sept. 25 the Commanders weren't considering surgery or an IR placement for Daniels.

Quinn said the same day the Commanders were considering Daniels "week-to-week" and that Marcus Mariota would start in Week 3 against the Seattle Seahawks. Mariota threw three touchdowns to help lead Washington to a 33-31 victory over the defending Super Bowl champs for the team's first win of the season.

Keeping Daniels off the injured reserve seemingly indicated the Commanders were hoping he might return within a four-game stretch.

The Commanders are scheduled to play home games against the Colts and New York Giants as well as a road game against the San Francisco 49ers over that span.

Daniels suffered the latest in what has been a series of injuries to his left elbow during the Commanders' Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

The quarterback's left arm bent awkwardly on a fall late in the first half of the Sept. 20 matchup. He was carted off the field and later returned to the sideline wearing an air cast.

Daniels previously suffered a dislocated left elbow in Week 9 of the 2025 season. He missed three games with the injury, then returned for Week 14 only to re-injure the elbow and sit out the rest of the season.

Mariota stepped in for Daniels following his injury but was unable to stop the Commanders from falling into an 0-2 hole to start the season. The veteran quarterback, who went 2-6 in eight starts for the Commanders last season, could once more be tasked with leading Washington's offense in the short term.

Still, it's encouraging that Daniels is making enough progress in his recovery to travel with the Commanders to London for Sunday's matchup against the Colts.

articles.title: De'Von Achane Injured, Latest on Dolphins RB's Timeline to Return & Ollie Gordon II Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane will miss the rest of the season after suffering a torn ACL during Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane will miss the rest of the season after suffering a torn ACL during Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .

The news comes after Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley expressed concern following the game:

Achane exited early in the first quarter before the Dolphins provided the update in the third.

Running back Jaylen Wright was ruled out ahead of the game due to a stinger and a foot injury.

Ollie Gordon II will be slated to lead the Dolphins' run game for the remainder of the Week 3 matchup.

Achane fell after an awkward tackle on a short run early in the Dolphins' opening offensive drive.

His last play of the game was an 11-yard run for a first down, after which he was slow to get up.

The running back is visiting the sideline medical tent before walking off the field under his own power.

Achane later returned to the Dolphins' sideline without pads but walking without a visible limp, per Melanie Collins of CBS.

Wright was limited throughout the week before he was ruled out of practice Friday with his injuries.

Hafley said Friday he was "confident" Gordon could take on a larger role in Wright's absence.

There will now be even more pressure on Gordon to step up for Achane, who went into Sunday having recorded a team-high 31 carries while tying for the Dolphins lead with seven catches.

Gordon, 22, played just 15 offensive snaps and 13 special teams snaps over the first two games of the season, over which he amassed three carries for seven yards.

He could have increased fantasy upside with Achane, who had been on the field for more than 80 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps so far this season, missing the rest of the year.

The Dolphins are also missing top wideout Caleb Douglas to an ankle injury. Malik Washington and Chris Bell could also see a bump in usage should the Dolphins focus on their passing game now that the team's top two running backs are sidelined.

articles.title: Drake Maye Looks Like He's Trying to Copycat Mahomes, Aaron Rodgers in Flag Football, Says NFL Coach
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye seems to have lost his luster in the eyes of NFL evaluators amid his regression to start the 2026 season.
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye seems to have lost his luster in the eyes of NFL evaluators amid his regression to start the 2026 season.

After Maye committed three turnovers in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an opposing coach who ripped the third-year signal-caller for having "erratic judgment — not poor, just erratic." The coach went on to bring up examples from the Patriots' 1-2 start to this year.

"(Against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2), he has a deep cross against the Mike linebacker," the coach said. "They have only three underneath defenders. He hangs the ball so much that the Mike linebacker miraculously gets into the play, chases it down and creates the interception."

Maye's decision-making has been in question since he inexplicably threw into tight coverage for a game-losing interception against the Seattle Seahawks in New England's season opener. He had another eye-popping mistake against the Jags on Sunday when he lost control of the ball while attempting a pass.

"He is in the red zone against Pittsburgh, and he doesn't have to, but he sprints up in the pocket, he meets the defender and slides for the sack," the coach said. "He literally sacks himself. (Sunday), he just muffs the ball while passing. Fumbled it and gave it to the other team."

The coach went on to say that he feels Maye has been trying to play the hero for the Patriots by emulating other quarterbacks who can thrive both in and out of the structure of the offense.

"The best players, their fundamentals are impeccable, repeatable. This guy's are not. He has nervous, happy feet. He does not throw off a sturdy platform. He is not real accurate on the move, and tries the heroics," the coach said. After a pause, he added, "He looks like he is watching (Patrick) Mahomes and (Aaron) Rodgers in primetime games and is at the flag football game on Saturday afternoon trying to play copycat."

The Patriots will need to get better play out of Maye if they hope to make a second straight run to the Super Bowl. Things won't get any easier for New England when it faces the AFC East rival Buffalo Bills (3-0) in Week 4.

articles.title: Despite popular narratives, free speech is working in Macklemore’s favor
articles.summary: Despite objections that a billionaire’s wealth shouldn’t “decide who gets to speak,” the system actually worked pretty well.
articles.body:
Almost everyone reveres freedom of speech in the abstract. Too often, however, enthusiasm rises and falls with the identity of the speaker and the subject matter of the speech.

A case in point is the widely reported controversy over comments by the rapper Macklemore, whose many pro-Palestine supporters have taken no interest in the expressive rights of anyone who disagrees with them.

Earlier this month, as an opening act for the much more famous Ed Sheeran at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, Macklemore delighted some Sheeran fans and upset others by interrupting his act with a repeated call to “Free Palestine,” to be spread “from Gaza all the way to the occupied West Bank.” During his next song, the large stadium screens showed a video with scenes of Gaza devastation and campus protests.

The reaction of the 80,000 people in the stands was relatively subdued. Some cheered, but most appeared to remain silent. That wasn’t the case outside the stadium, as viral replays of Macklemore’s declaration sparked outrage among certain Israel supporters who objected to the rapper’s “one-sided” imagery.

Robert Kraft, the owner of the NFL’s New England Patriots and the Gillette Stadium, announced that he would cancel Sheeran’s upcoming concert unless Macklemore was dropped from the lineup. Other owners joined in Kraft’s demand .

Sheeran’s promoter acquiesced, and Macklemore was removed from the tour. In response, all four of Sheeran’s other supporting acts withdrew in protest of the “silencing of Macklemore.” Other performers also sharply criticized Kraft’s interference with the concert tour.

The First Amendment itself does not apply to Kraft’s dictate. As a private owner, he has no obligation to make the Gillette Stadium available for speeches he finds objectionable or abhorrent, whether he happens to be right or wrong about Macklemore’s history of performing in a classically anti-Jewish caricature costume.

The First Amendment would apply if Macklemore had also been banned by publicly owned stadiums , where several future concerts are scheduled, but that does not appear to have happened. Instead, it was Sheeran’s tour promoter , a private company called the Messina Group, that evidently bowed to pressure in a futile attempt to avoid controversy.

At Sheeran’s following concert, where he performed alone, he apologized for “making mistakes” in the Macklemore incident. Explaining that he never wanted to be an “activist musician,” Sheeran said, “What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate. My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and the loss of civilians’ lives, of children’s lives.”

Free speech, of course, is a broader concept than the First Amendment. Macklemore has indeed been deprived of the huge audiences on Sheeran’s tour, but he otherwise remains quite free to rally support for Palestine anywhere else, whenever and however he chooses to.

If anything, his message has been amplified by the many other musicians who have spoken out in his support. Last week, Macklemore announced plans for his own “Free Palestine” tour, to begin in October in cities across Europe and the U.S.

Despite objections that a billionaire’s wealth shouldn’t “decide who gets to speak,” the system actually worked pretty well. Kraft controlled his own property, without permitting its use for ideas that he rejects. The time-honored response, well known to civil libertarians, was to generate “ more speech ” from many voices, projecting Macklemore’s message well beyond the confines of Gillette Stadium.

The irony, however, is that boycotts much more extensive than Kraft’s have been internationally deployed against Jewish and Israeli performers for years, with virtually no objection from the broader arts community.

The Orthodox Jewish reggae artist Matisyahu has repeatedly had concerts threatened or canceled under pressure from pro-Palestine activists, for the apparent offense of performing under a Hebrew name. He was not the only one .

Jewish comedians have had shows canceled in the U.S. and at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in Scotland, the latter resulting in a court finding that it constituted unlawful religious discrimination. Poets , authors , novelists, graphic artists and actors have been boycotted, deplatformed or disrupted because they were deemed insufficiently anti-Israel.

None of these cases, among many others, attracted even a small fraction of the national attention devoted to Macklemore’s exclusion from Gillette Stadium. Almost nobody outside the Jewish community has spoken up for artists who have been all but blacklisted, in some cases due to their identification with Israel, and in other cases only because of their perceived silence on Gaza.

If Macklemore himself ever objected to censoring Israeli and Jewish performers, I have found no record of it. Among musicians, who should know better, free speech has been defended only for approved speakers.

Addressing a recent bar conference in Oklahoma, Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor explained that her “greatest fear” for the future of American democracy is the “lack of quality in our teaching of civics education.” In particular, she worried that people “don’t understand what the First Amendment means.”

Steven Lubet is the Williams Memorial Professor Emeritus at the Northwestern University Pritzker School of Law. He is coauthor of “Judicial Conduct and Ethics.”

articles.title: Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield will miss 3 weeks with dislocated thumb as coach Todd Bowles' seat gets hotter
articles.summary: Mayfield at least avoided a more serious injury.
articles.body:
A few coaches were on early hot-seat watch after just a couple games.

Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen helped himself with a win over the Houston Texans. As did Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn with an upset victory over the Seattle Seahawks .

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-3 after a home loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and it cost them more than just another lost game. Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb on his final pass — an interception after he scrambled on fourth down in the final two minutes — and will miss three weeks, Bowles announced on Monday. Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels, replaced Mayfield for the final 28 seconds on Sunday, is expected to start in his place.

An MRI revealed no ligament damage or a fracture, which would have lengthened Mayfield's absence.

Mayfield was holding his right hand in obvious pain after it was hit on the follow through of his pass. When he walked off the field, he held his hand until he got to the sideline. Mayfield went straight back to the locker room even though there was a chance for Tampa Bay to get the ball back.

And the Buccaneers did get it back after a field goal. Daniels replaced Mayfield and threw an interception on a Hail Mary as the Vikings held on for the 23-16 win.

With Mayfield missing time, it makes it even harder for Bowles and the Bucs to dig out of their hole. The Bucs are a highly disappointing 2-10 in their past 12 games going back to last season. And once again, the Bucs had the look of a team that is not playing anywhere near its talent level.

Sunday's loss had more sloppy mistakes that have become the norm for the Bucs under Bowles. They gave up an 86-yard punt return TD to fall behind 10-0. A 41-yard touchdown catch by Jordan Addison gave Minnesota a 17-10 lead. A holding penalty wiped out an amazing 85-yard touchdown by Chris Godwin Jr.

After the Buccaneers got an fortunate unnecessary roughness call on a third down, Mayfield and Bucky Irving ran into each other on a handoff for a 6-yard loss and Tampa Bay had to settle for a field goal on that drive. Their entire offense was unprepared to do anything against the Vikings' constant blitzes, including on the final fourth-and-13 when Mayfield had to retreat under pressure and throw a desperation pass that had no shot.

The Buccaneers had a great shot to win because the Vikings' offense wasn't capable of putting the game away. Kyler Murray, returning to the lineup for the first time since suffering a concussion early in the season opener, was ineffective. He completed just eight of his first 21 passes.

Justin Jefferson left the game early with an ankle injury and that didn't help, but overall the Vikings offense had plenty of issues. Over one 10-possession stretch they punted eight times and threw an interception, a ball that was batted at the line by Vita Vea and ended up being hauled in by A'Shawn Robinson.

But the Vikings got the win. They're 3-0. The Buccaneers are on the opposite end at 0-3. And if it doesn't turn around fast — which will be difficult without Mayfield — the Buccaneers could be having to ask some tough questions about their head coach.

articles.title: Jalon Daniels, Emeka Egbuka, Bucky Irving's Fantasy Outlook After Baker Mayfield's Injury
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers who relied on Baker Mayfield will have to turn elsewhere for the immediate future, but the thumb injury he suffered during Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings will also impact the fantasy production of others on the roster.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers who relied on Baker Mayfield will have to turn elsewhere for the immediate future, but the thumb injury he suffered during Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings will also impact the fantasy production of others on the roster.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Monday that Mayfield will miss at least three weeks, while ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Jalon Daniels will be the new starter.

Daniels will have to prove himself in an NFL offense before fantasy managers put him in their starting lineups, but his rushing ability and preseason performances mean he is worth at least a waiver-wire pickup.

As for top playmakers Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving, it is not time for fantasy managers to panic even if their ceilings are lower without Mayfield leading the way. It would be anything but a surprise if the Buccaneers simplify the offense for Daniels, which could mean just getting the ball into the hands of Egbuka and Irving as quickly as possible and letting them go to work.

That means their floors should still be safe, so keep them in your starting lineups.

In addition to getting the ball to Egbuka and Irving, part of those gameplans could include asking Daniels to use his legs.

And how effectively he does so will determine his fantasy ceiling.

He tallied 14 carries in three preseason games and scored a touchdown on the ground during a win over the New York Jets. He also went 10-of-15 passing for 111 yards in that contest.

Throw in a touchdown pass in Tampa Bay's preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs, and Daniels went from undrafted free agent to the team's backup.

That turned out to be an important development with Mayfield suffering an injury so early in the season.

With no regular-season track record to fall back on when it comes to Daniels, fantasy football managers should approach the situation with some caution. But an impressive performance in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers could clear the way for him to become a realistic starting option in Week 5 against a Dallas Cowboys defense that is 25th in the league in points allowed per game.

There is much more of a track record when it comes to Egbuka and Irving, so there shouldn't be any changes there when it comes to fantasy strategy.

But managers shouldn't be surprised if they are slightly less effective with a backup quarterback running the show.

articles.title: First major trade of NFL season is here as Giants acquire JJ McCarthy from Vikings
articles.summary: The New York Giants acquired quarterback JJ McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings after Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the rest of the regular season.
articles.body: The New York Giants acquired quarterback JJ McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 fifth-round pick, adding another young player at the most important position in football less than a week after learning Jaxson Dart would be out for at least the rest of the regular season. The Vikings announced the trade Monday pending McCarthy passing a physical. Dart had surgery last week on his left knee after getting injured early in a loss at the Los Angeles Rams. Jameis Winston started and the Giants beat Tennessee on Sunday, despite not scoring a touchdown and having just 238 yards of offense. Coach John Harbaugh said afterward that Winston would get the nod again this Sunday against Arizona but hinted that the Giants were not content to stand pat in Dart’s absence. “The plans are the plans,” Harbaugh said. “The opportunities that you have are the opportunities you have. No matter what, we’re going to do everything we can to make our team as strong as we can based on what options we have.” The first opportunity turned out to be adding McCarthy, the 10th pick in the 2024 draft who lost the starting job in Minnesota to Kyler Murray and fell behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart. McCarthy started 10 games last season, completing 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. McCarthy missed what would have been his rookie season after injuring his right knee. He was picked a year ahead of Dart, but each was born in 2003, with McCarthy being just four months older. Long term, that sets up a fascinating situation for New York. For now, McCarthy provides competition for Winston, and it’s not out of the realm of possibility that another QB is added to the mix. The Vikings sold low on a player who led Michigan to the national title in his final college season and was once considered a big part of Minnesota’s future.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy: New York Giants trade for Minnesota Vikings quarterback after Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart was recently ruled out for the rest of the 2026 NFL season after suffering a knee injury that requires surgery against the Los Angeles Rams in Week Two; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI
articles.body:
Dart suffered a year-ending knee injury early in New York's Week Two defeat to the Los Angeles Rams as they begin a new chapter in their first season under head coach John Harbaugh.

Veteran Jameis Winston replaced Dart under center and started on Sunday as the Giants beat the Tennessee Titans to improve to 2-1 on the year.

NFL Network reported that the Giants are trading a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings in exchange for McCarthy, who was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 Draft.

For more than one reason McCarthy has failed to establish himself as Minnesota's starter since being drafted out of Michigan, where he played under Jim Harbaugh, brother of Giants head coach John.

He suffered a year-ending injury in preseason of his rookie campaign, paving the way for Sam Darnold to launch his career revival by spearheading Kevin O'Connell's side to an unlikely playoff berth.

Darnold departed the following offseason to sign with the Seattle Seahawks, opening the door for McCarthy to get his Vikings career up and running upon his return to full health.

McCarthy marked his NFL debut by helping the Vikings overturn an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chicago Bears in Week One of the 2025 season. He threw two interceptions against the Atlanta Falcons the following week, during which he suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out of the next five weeks.

Carson Wentz impressed in his absence before McCarthy returned to face the Detroit Lions in Week Nine, only for further issues to disrupt the remainder of his season.

This past offseason he lost the Vikings starting to veteran acquisition Kyler Murray, before falling to third string behind Wentz.

He leaves the Vikings with a record of 6-4, his last appearance coming against the Baltimore Ravens in preseason in August.

The Giants had entered the season enthused by a fresh start under Harbaugh, who left the Ravens after 18 seasons earlier this year. That hope was only strengthened in Week One as Dart led the Giants to a statement win over the Dallas Cowboys.

Dart, the 25th overall pick in 2025, had galvanised a Giants team with just two winning seasons since 2016, supported by a star wide receiver in Malik Nabers, a revamped offensive line, running back Cam Skattebo and a talent-rich pass rush. articles.title: Giants acquire J.J. McCarthy from Vikings for 2027 fifth-round pick
articles.summary: New York adds depth after Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the season due to a knee injury.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are acquiring quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

McCarthy had been serving as the third-string quarterback in Minnesota behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz . New York adds depth at quarterback after starter Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the remainder of the regular season due to a torn MCL and meniscus.

New York started veteran Jameis Winston and called up Jake Haener to serve as his backup in the Week 3 win over the Titans. Even though the Giants picked up their second win of the season, Winston struggled, and New York's 12 points were from four field goals.

With the acquisition, the Giants have waived Haener and intend to bring him back on the practice squad. It seems that the intention is for McCarthy to, at worst, back up Winston in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals .

This move gets McCarthy a fresh start as the 23-year-old is still in just his third year in the league. The former Michigan Wolverine played for Jim Harbaugh in college and will now play for his brother, John Harbaugh, with the Giants.

McCarthy missed his entire rookie season due to a torn MCL that he suffered in the 2024 NFL preseason. Last year, made his regular-season debut, going 6-4 over his 10 starts. The QB finished with 1,632 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. Injuries also continued to plague McCarthy in his second season, missing five games with a high-ankle sprain and another game down the stretch with a concussion.

Winston took over for Dart during the team's 28-6 loss to the Rams . He struggled mightily, completing only 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards. The 32-year-old Winston was sacked twice and threw a second-quarter interception while in the red zone.

A backup for the last several years, Winston was once the top pick in the draft, back in 2015. That marked the beginning of his five-season run as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' QB1. Winston, a Heisman Trophy and national championship winner at Florida State, earned Pro Bowl honors as a rookie and led the NFL with 5,109 passing yards in 2019. That season, though, he infamously tossed 30 interceptions to go along with his 33 touchdown strikes.

On-field decision-making has held back Winston throughout his pro career. The Winston experience is a roller coaster, for better or worse. He can chuck the ball around the yard, as evidenced by his 25,021 career passing yards — a total he previously added to amid stints with the New Orleans Saints (2020-23) and Cleveland Browns (2024) before he joined the Giants ahead of last season — but he's notoriously turnover-prone.

That said, he's known for his infectious personality, unrelenting positivity as a leader and for his ability to spark an offense. Earlier this month, the Giants inked Winston to a two-year extension through 2028 that's reportedly worth $13 million . Harbaugh has gone to bat for the veteran this week.

"He can throw it," Harbaugh said last Wednesday of Winston . "He's a big, strong passing quarterback. He can throw the ball. Everybody that follows football has certainly seen Jameis play, and his strengths are evident.

Winston finished the Week 3 win going 14 of 22 passing for 118 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. He scrambled twice for 14 yards and was sacked three times.

New York has four more games until its Week 8 bye week. That could be when, depending on how Winston plays over the next month, the Giants could make a move to get McCarthy under center.

NEW YORK (AP) — The NFL has asked the Department of Homeland Security to take down a video on social media showing highlights of Hall of Fame safety Brian Dawkins in reference to a purported caravan of immigrants approaching the U.S. border.

The video posted on Sunday shows Dawkins' pregame walkout as he chants "The time has come," followed by a series of big hits. The DHS post includes the caption "Our time has come."

articles.title: Minter Explains How NFL Rule Impacted Ravens' Surprising Win vs. Cowboys amid Controversial Decision
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens used some late magic to defeat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in Sunday's NFL Rio Game, and head coach Jesse Minter explained how a recent rule change helped them to pull it off.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens used some late magic to defeat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in Sunday's NFL Rio Game, and head coach Jesse Minter explained how a recent rule change helped them to pull it off.

While speaking to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer after the victory, Minter discussed how the rule that a touchback into the end zone now puts the ball at the 35-yard line gave the Ravens just enough time to get into field-goal range.

"I thought they may just kick it down there, which makes your returner use some time, which then we would have probably kneeled it out and went to overtime," Minter told Breer. "You also risk a return, so I understand the touchback theory. But with the rules, I mean, there's a six-second play, really, to try to get the 20 yards or so needed to get in range. And it's really not a high risk, because they're going to be playing to prevent that. It's not like you're going to be throwing into a ton of traffic. And if it's incomplete, you go to overtime."

After tying the game at 31-31, the Cowboys kicked the ball into the end zone with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter. While Minter said he normally would need all seven seconds to pull off a play to get into field-goal range, star quarterback Lamar Jackson and wide receiver Zay Flowers were able to connect quickly before Flowers used Baltimore's last timeout with one second left on the clock, setting up Tyler Loop's game-winning 56-yard field goal.

"It's knowing where the line is, knowing that as soon as you catch it, you've got to get down," Minter said. "You can't catch it and feel like you've got space and try to gain a couple more yards because you'll run out of time. So, just a great job by him and Lamar putting the ball where it needed to be for us to be able to execute that."

Minter praised Jackson, Flowers and the rest of his team for having situational awareness and executing efficiently to end the game.

"Really cool," Minter said. "Really cool. … Just great execution by Zay, running the route to perfection, running to the right depth. Lamar, obviously, making a great throw on time, which is super important. And a major shout-out to our game management crew—we've repped those situations a lot, and you wait for them to come up, and it comes up, and the guys are ready to do it."

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs: How special Travis Kelce and 'secret sauce' Kenneth Walker are inspiring Patrick Mahomes resurgence
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold discuss the immediate impact of Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI
articles.body:
The Chiefs extended their perfect start to 3-0 on Sunday as they defeated the Miami Dolphins 24-10 in their bid to return to the playoffs, having missed out for the first time since 2014 last season.

Former Seattle Seahawks running back Walker has made an immediate impact since the Super Bowl MVP signed a three-year $45m deal in free agency.

While Walker leads the NFL with 360 rushing yards, Mahomes has shown signs of rediscovering his devastating best after returning from last December's season-ending knee injury.

"I think Patrick right now is just getting used to people around his legs," said Reinebold on Inside the Huddle. "You're in that vortex of violence that is called the pocket, I just think that he's getting more confident, he slides around in the pocket a little bit more than he did early.

"And Travis Kelce, man. Every time I think the guy's done, he makes a play. He is really, really special.

"And Kenneth Walker to me is the secret sauce now. That could be the dynamic that they haven't had where they were so reliant on Patrick and Kelce to make plays. Even though he statistically didn't have a great game, but you saw his impact on the game, especially when they got into short yardage situations."

Walker finished Sunday's win over the Titans with 18 carries for 70 yards and a touchdown, his threat making a notable difference in allowing the Chiefs to enjoy success out of an increased usage of play-action.

"One thing we talked about early in the season last year was there was no running game from the Chiefs and the only running really came from Patrick Mahomes taking off and going downfield and risking life and limb," said Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds.

"We said that you can do that for a short period of time and lo and behold, he tears his knee ligaments late in the season. Just sometimes just that threat of Kenneth Walker means that Mahomes doesn't have to do that, it's going to stand the Chiefs in good stead in December and January."

Kelce has meanwhile started the season with 14 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns after signing a contract extension with the Chiefs in the offseason amid suggestions he might retire. Based on early weeks, the tight end has no plans to walk away just yet.

"The dynamic of having a back like Walker, especially one who can run so well between the tackles, and then pairing that with a tight end like Kelce, and then one of the top quarterbacks like Mahomes, it makes the Chiefs a really dynamic offense," Reinebold continued.

"Andy (Reid) dials him up. He went back to the shovel pass on the goal, and that underhanded shovel pass, he is something. He is a football guy's football guy, I bet he has on his desk a notepad of little yellow sticky notes with plays."

Next up the Chiefs face their divisional rival Las Vegas Raiders, who are also 3-0 on the year after Sunday's win over the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: Breece Hall Injured, Latest Rumors on Jets RB's Timeline to Return & Braelon Allen Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: New York Jets running back Breece Hall is considered week-to-week after exiting Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions with a quad injury, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
New York Jets running back Breece Hall is considered week-to-week after exiting Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions with a quad injury, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter.

That leaves Braelon Allen atop the depth chart at the position, with Isaiah Davis also available.

Hall, 25, suffered the injury after being tackled and twisted out of bounds, near the end zone, during the fourth quarter. He appeared to land hard on his right leg. He had rushed 13 times for 32 yards and caught three passes for 23 yards before the injury.

He has been clearly atop the pecking order in New York's backfield this season and was putting up low-end RB1 numbers. That makes his loss a big one for both the Jets and fantasy players who drafted him.

It opens the door for Allen from a fantasy perspective, however, making him a must-add player on waivers this week. Coming into Sunday he had rushed for 457 yards and four touchdowns in 23 career games across parts of three seasons in what has primarily been a complementary role to Hall.

Allen is rostered in just 18 percent of Yahoo leagues, so he likely will be available. Anyone who has him on the roster will have to prioritize him on waivers, but if you are low on options at running back or flex, he's a fantastic target.

Granted, much will depend on how long Hall is sidelined for. If Hall is looking at any sort of extended stint on the sidelines, Allen is going to be the most popular addition in fantasy football this week. Consider him a very solid flex option if he's forced into starting duty.

articles.title: The NFL has officially become flag football, fans are fuming & MLB makes a baffling call ahead of the playoffs
articles.summary: The final Monday of September brings NFL officiating outrage after a textbook quarterback hit drew a flag in the Chiefs-Dolphins fourth quarter.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Final Monday of September. This is it, folks. We're a few days away from October. First full month of football just about in the books. And now we have the MLB postseason on deck?! Along with more football? How lucky are we? What a country. Goodness, we are blessed. Solid weekend of sports, right? The golf world is breathing a sigh of relief today after the fellas avoided a catastrophe yesterday. The college football world was, once again, treated to absolute cinema for about 12 hours on Saturday. I actually thought the NFL had a really nice bounce back Sunday after a lackluster Week 2 ... Except for the officiating. It completely ruined everything, as it tends to do. It was just bad call after bad call. I was stunned at what I saw in yesterday's Dolphins-Chiefs game. Stunned. Somehow, it got even worse in last night's thriller in Denver. It's just so, unfathomably bad at this point. And there is no accountability. It's disgusting. We'll dive in here in a bit. But first, welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where you officially cannot touch, breath, or even look at a quarterback in the National Football League anymore. Sad. NFL WEEK 3 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: PATRIOTS HAVE A MAYE PROBLEM, CHARGERS HIT ROCK BOTTOM AND COWBOYS CRUMBLE What else? I've got Cam Ward being quite possibly the biggest bust of my lifetime, a ballboy in Jacksonville picking a fight with a massive defensive end over a football, and how about the BS move Major League Baseball pulled this weekend? Is Manfred serious with this? What a joke. You'll see. OK, let's get this class — and week — started. It's a Monday night, after all. We've got MORE football to watch. Grab you a beer for National Drink Beer Day (solid holiday!) and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! I couldn't believe my eyes in yesterday's Chiefs-Dolphins game Let's go ahead and jump right in. No beating around the bush on this final Monday of September. So, the horrible Miami Dolphins lost to the not-horrible Kansas City Chiefs yesterday in a game that was surprisingly close. Credit to Miami for looking markedly better. Credit to the Chiefs for still covering the spread. Win-win! Miami actually had a legit shot to win this game, believe it or not. Trailing 17-10 to start the fourth quarter, the Dolphins had the Chiefs backed up into their own end zone on third and long. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass, and was absolutely crushed by Chop Robinson, forcing an incomplete pass. It looked like a textbook quarterback hit, which is nearly impossible to do given the ridiculous rules nowadays. Helmet to the chest, and putting the arms out on the way down to catch himself as to not land on Mahomes with his full body weight. Again — stupid rules — but Chop appeared to follow them to a tee ... Key word there being "appeared." The Cam Ward era in Tennessee is going well What are we doing here? Seriously. It's just so silly at this point. If that's a penalty, the defenders truly have no chance in this league. None. WHAT is he supposed to have done differently? And by the way, I'm not saying it was the wrong call. It wasn't. It was the right call. The RULE itself is mind-numbingly stupid. Here's Rule 12, Section 2, Article 11(b) in the NFL rulebook: A rushing defender is prohibited from committing such intimidating and punishing acts as "stuffing" a passer into the ground or unnecessarily wrestling or driving him down after the passer has thrown the ball, even if the rusher makes his initial contact with the passer within the one-step limitation provided for in (a) above. When tackling a passer who is in a defenseless posture (i.e. before, during, or after throwing or attempting a pass), a defensive player must not unnecessarily or violently throw him down or land on top of him with all or most of the defender’s weight. Instead, the defensive player must strive to fall to the side of the passer’s body, or to brace his fall with his arms to avoid landing on the passer with all or most of his body weight. It's just such a silly rule. "All or most of his body weight." What does that even mean? That's the most subjective rule I've ever seen. How does a ref determine how much body weight one is falling with? Between this and the ridiculous pass interference call that cost the Rams the game last night, it was just a really poor Sunday for NFL refs. And I mean REALLY poor: Just horrible. I said it last year. I said it the year before. I've said it every year for a decade now: NFL officiating is ruining the game. So are the rules. It's insane. Frankly, it's sad. OK, let's move it along and check in with last year's first overall pick, Cam Ward! Speaking of bad NFL Sundays ... Jags, more Jags & MLB's totally fair move! I've never seen a quarterback do that before. Ever. What is that? Cam Ward, by the way, is now 3-17 as a starter. Pretty big sample size at this point. And he's still acting like THAT? Hey, buddy, why don't you RUN if there's that much time back there and you're bored? Ever think about that? Maybe do a little scrambling and figure something out? Same with the goal line play at the end. He had the pylon right in front of him. Just keep running! Instead, he just throws a duck to the Giants and it was curtains. The No. 2 pick behind Ward last year? That would be Travis Hunter. Speaking of Hunter, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big night of FOOTBALL. Congrats on your first career INT, Travis! Just a weird Sunday in the NFL, right? What's going on here? Why is this guy getting so defensive? "Hey! Don't touch me! Do not touch me!" he says as he tries to slap 6-foot-5, 255-pound Josh Hines-Allen away. Good luck, pal. You're gonna need it! Here's the best part ... that wasn't even the weirdest part of that game yesterday! Anyone see what Trevor Lawrence pulled with 8 minutes left? Couple things here ... CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OK, on the way out, let's quickly check in on how Major League Baseball treated the final Sunday of the season for the Red Sox and Yankees ahead of their Wild Card Series this week: For those who missed it, the Red Sox and Cubs had to fly to Florida to play Game 162 at Tropicana Field yesterday. It was a meaningless game, as both teams had already clinched everything they could clinch. The Yanks and Orioles, meanwhile, got rained out and MLB told them not to worry about it. Okeedokee! Makes sense. Whatever. MLB postseason starts tomorrow. Four games, all day long, beginning at 2 p.m. with Braves-Phils. Can't wait. Nothing better than some playoff baseball. Sox in 3. Now, let's have a week.

articles.title: Three generations found love through the Kansas City Chiefs: The heartwarming story behind the Hunt family
articles.summary: For the Hunt family, the Kansas City Chiefs have always been about more than football.
articles.body: For the Hunt family, the Kansas City Chiefs have always been about more than football. The franchise has been woven into the family's history for decades through championships, family traditions, milestone moments, and, remarkably, love stories. Now, with Gracie Hunt preparing to marry Derek Green, the son of former Chiefs quarterback Trent Green, that connection has taken on an almost storybook quality.Gracie recently posted a reel on how she and Derek represent the “third generation” of a Chiefs love story, bringing attention to a remarkable family thread that stretches back to the franchise's earliest days. It is a story that begins with Lamar and Norma Hunt, continues with Clark and Tavia Hunt, and now reaches Gracie and Derek.Three generations. One football team. And an extraordinary number of family ties connecting them.Long before Gracie and Derek: The Chiefs love story that began with Lamar and Norma HuntLong before Gracie Hunt was born, her grandfather Lamar Hunt was building the football franchise that would eventually become one of the NFL's most recognizable organizations.Hunt founded the franchise in 1959 as the Dallas Texans, one of the original American Football League teams. The club relocated to Kansas City in 1963 and became the Kansas City Chiefs.Norma Hunt was part of that early chapter, working as a hostess for the Dallas Texans while also helping sell season tickets. Lamar and Norma married in 1964, shortly after the franchise's move to Kansas City.Their marriage became one of the foundational relationships of the Hunt family. Norma would go on to become one of the most recognizable figures associated with the Chiefs and remained closely connected to the organization throughout her life. She was famously the only woman to attend every Super Bowl from the first game through Super Bowl LVII.Their son Clark would eventually inherit a central role in the family business and become the Chiefs' chairman and CEO. And years later, another Hunt love story would begin inside the organization.Then came Clark and Tavia HuntGracie's parents, Clark and Tavia Hunt, have their own Chiefs-origin love story.Tavia was working as a college intern in the Chiefs' public relations department in 1991 when she met Clark. Their first meeting eventually developed into a relationship, and the two married and built a family of their own. There is an especially touching detail from the early days of their relationship.Tavia has recalled that roughly six weeks after they began dating, Clark gave her a postcard that his mother Norma had previously given him. Clark told Tavia that he hoped he had found the person with whom he could travel through life.Tavia has said she still keeps that postcard framed. In retrospect, the moment feels almost symbolic. A message passed from one generation to the next, connecting Norma's story with Clark and Tavia's.And eventually, it would become part of Gracie's story, too.Gracie and Derek's story began before they even knew what it meantGracie's relationship with Derek Green has another remarkable layer.Derek isn't simply the son of a former NFL player. His father, Trent Green, spent six seasons as the Chiefs' quarterback from 2001 through 2006. That meant Gracie and Derek grew up around the same Chiefs world.In fact, they knew each other as children. Gracie has said that she and Derek would play together as babies during the Chiefs' Christmas parties. At the time, of course, neither could have known that those childhood encounters would eventually become the beginning of their own love story.Their families were already intertwined with the organization from different sides. Gracie was growing up as part of the Hunt family. Derek was growing up as the son of one of the team's quarterbacks.The Chiefs were the common thread.Years later, they found each other againTheir childhood connection might have remained just a sweet family memory if they hadn't crossed paths again years later. In 2017, Gracie and Derek reconnected on the sidelines before a Chiefs game at Arrowhead Stadium.Years later, Gracie would describe their connection using a phrase that made the story feel even more poetic: an “invisible string.” When she eventually shared their relationship publicly, she referenced the fact that they had met at Arrowhead years earlier and suggested that something had been quietly connecting them all along.What began as a childhood friendship eventually became a romance. The couple went public with their relationship in 2025, and Gracie described Derek as her best friend.Then came the next chapter. On April 4, 2026, Derek proposed to Gracie.The engagement brought the two families together once again, with their parents present for the celebration. Gracie shared the news with the words “It was always you,” while Derek responded, “FOREVER AND EVER.”Even the engagement ring carried a family connection.The emerald-cut ring featured a green center stone, a fitting detail for someone marrying into the Green family. More importantly, Gracie has spoken about the significance of the people and relationships surrounding the ring and the proposal.And then, after their engagement celebration in August, Gracie and Derek returned to Arrowhead Stadium, the very place where their adult story had begun.Gracie described the moment with words that captured the circular nature of their journey:“Of all the places, all the moments — God wrote our story to begin right here.”There was something fitting about them returning to the stadium together as an engaged couple. They had first been children in the orbit of the Chiefs. Then friends. Then two people who found their way back to each other.And now they were standing on the same ground as they prepared to start a family of their own.The Chiefs connection runs on both sidesWhat makes Gracie and Derek's relationship particularly unusual is that the Chiefs are part of their story from both sides. Gracie is the granddaughter of the man who founded the franchise and the daughter of its current chairman and CEO.Derek is the son of Trent Green, who became one of the most accomplished quarterbacks in Chiefs history during his six seasons with the organization.Even more poignantly, Gracie has revealed that Derek's father has been connected to her family for years beyond football. In discussing their relationship, she noted that Trent Green even spoke at her grandfather Lamar Hunt's funeral.That detail makes the phrase “three generations, one team” feel less like a catchy caption and more like an accurate description of how deeply these families' lives have overlapped.Three generations. One team. articles.title: NFL asks US Homeland Security to remove video with former star player
articles.summary: Agency used video of Hall of Fame player Brian Dawkins to show readiness for border protection.
articles.body:
The National Football League (NFL) has asked the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to stop using a video of a retired star player on social media, after the agency used highlights of his career to show its readiness to protect the United States border against a purported caravan of immigrants that was heading towards it.

“The league has requested the DHS take down the video,” NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said on Monday.

The video, posted on Sunday, shows Brian Dawkins, a former player for the Philadelphia Eagles and Denver Broncos, walking out before a game and chanting “the time has come”. It then features a montage of him tackling opposing players on the field, set to heavy metal music. The DHS post includes the caption: “Our time has come.”

Dawkins was a highly celebrated NFL player who retired in 2011 after playing 16 seasons in the NFL.

US President Donald Trump has made immigration a central part of his second term in office, terming the inflow of migrants across the border from Mexico an “invasion” and deploying federal forces in cities across the country to round up undocumented people.

During his first term, Trump deployed thousands of troops along the border with Mexico to stop a caravan of Central American migrants who had been making their way north. Critics called the deployment a vast overreaction and dismissed it as a political stunt ahead of the 2018 midterm elections.

articles.title: 49ers Trade Pitch Brings Back History-Making Wide Receiver
articles.summary: Sports Illustrated's Grant Cohn believes the 49ers should bring back history-making wide receiver. The post 49ers Trade Pitch Brings Back History-Making Wide...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers might need to start thinking outside the box when it comes to filling out their wide receiver room.

With starter Mike Evans going down with a rib injury in a Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals , 49ers on SI's Grant Cohn believes the time has come to make a move.

"The 49ers should trade a 7th-round pick to Minnesota for Jauan Jennings ," Cohn wrote on his official X account on Monday. "They need him, and he needs them."

Jennings was a 7th-round pick (No. 217 overall) by the 49ers in the 2020 NFL Draft and played his 1st 6 seasons in San Francisco — including making history in an overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LVIII when he became just the 2nd player in NFL history to throw for a touchdown and catch a touchdown pass in the Super Bowl, and 1 of just 6 non-quarterbacks to throw a touchdown pass in Super Bowl history.

Jennings had career highs of 77 receptions for 975 yards and 6 touchdowns in 15 games for the 49ers in 2024 and followed that up with 55 receptions for 643 yards and a career-high 9 touchdowns in 15 games in 2025.

Growing Drumbeat for 49ers to Bring Back Jennings

With the 49ers sitting at 3-0 but with dwindling resources at wide receiver, Niner's Noise's Nick San Miguel also thinks a trade for Jennings might be the answer.

"The San Francisco 49ers seemingly lose a new wide receiver every week," San Miguel wrote on September 26. "In Week 1, it was De'Zhaun Stribling, and in Week 2, it was Demarcus Robinson . While neither player should be out for the season, it's still concerning and the Niners made a move by signing veteran Brandin Cooks to the practice squad. Jauan Jennings might just be one of their most logical options, especially with how poorly his start with the Minnesota Vikings has gone. Obviously, it's only been two games but Jennings only got one target in Week 1 and then missed Week 2 because of a personal matter. That's way too small of a sample size to say he is a bust or anything, but if he never materializes into a viable target with Minnesota, then a return to San Francisco would make all the sense in the world."

Jauan Jennings Missed Out on Big-Money Contract

Jennings entered the 2026 offseason with his eyes on a big prize — Spotrac projected his market value was in the realm of a 3-year, $67 million free-agent contract.

That deal never materialized, and Jennings finally agreed to a 1-year, $8 million contract with the Minnesota Vikings on May 11 — some 2 months after the start of the NFL's free-agent cycle.

Jennings requested that the 49ers trade him before the 2025 season, and the franchise signed his replacement on the 1st day of the 2026 free-agent cycle, luring Evans away from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a 3-year, $42.5 million contract.

ESPN's Matt Bowen has Jennings ranked as the No. 1 free agent still available on April 8.

"At 6-foot-3, 213 pounds, Jennings is a consistent route runner who plays through contact and makes himself available to the quarterback on in-breaking targets," Bowen wrote. "He caught 55 passes last season for an injury-riddled 49ers unit, scoring nine touchdowns. Jennings was even better in 2024, when he ranked 12th in ESPN's receiver scores and had 975 receiving yards."

articles.title: Mike Evans Injury, Latest Updates on 49ers WR's Timeline to Return After Being Carted Off
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is day-to-day after exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is day-to-day after exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

After a particularly big hit, the six-time Pro Bowler appeared to be holding his right midsection. He was soon carted to the locker room.

He was subsequently ruled out from the game with a rib injury.

The injuries are starting to pile up for San Francisco. Within the receiver room alone, Demarcus Robinson and second-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling are on injured reserve. Stribling won't be back until potentially November.

Evans was putting together a solid performance as well. He caught three passes for 34 yards and found the end zone on a 23-yard touchdown grab.

The Niners didn't have any trouble moving the ball against Arizona. The Cardinals opened with a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, but their last two games are more of what fans expected from them.

Evans' injury didn't have much impact on Sunday's outcome. Looking beyond Week 3, San Francisco can't keep seeing its receivers go down.

Aside from his All-Pro season in 2021, Deebo Samuel Sr. hasn't been a consistent No. 1 option. Take Stribling and Evans out of the mix and the depth at wideout falls off dramatically.

Especially with matchups against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks ahead, coach Kyle Shanahan will hope Evans won't have to miss additional time.
